policy: Classifications annotate exact source claims without removing, merging or privileging a candidate. Shared genealogical components are legitimate contextual co-references, not two possible readings of one person's identity; unresolved cases must remain unresolved.

cases.reason: The pinned Greek word Βαριωνᾶ (Bar-Jonah), a single fused patronymic in Matthew 16:17, directly addresses Simon Peter while embedding the name of his father Jonah. This source word can legitimately point to both the son and his father as a name component; it does NOT claim those two men are identical or represent two competing identities. The separately debated historical relationship of John/Jonah as a father's name (John 1:42; 21:15–17 vs Matthew 16:17) remains a textual/name-form question and is not certified by this overlap classification.

cases.reason: Ezra 3:9's exact Masoretic word is יְהוּדָה (Judah), as the ancestor in the family expression 'sons of Judah' rather than an explicit spelling of Hodaviah or Hodiah. Ezra 2:40 and Nehemiah 7:43 instead name the Levitical family as Hodaviah/Hodevah. Some scholarship treats Judah as an alternate reading/name for Hodaviah; other textual criticism argues for a scribal misreading, not two securely identical individuals. Frozen Hodiah.2 also claims this word while its other named witnesses occur in Nehemiah. The original name tokens cannot prove Hodiah.2 = Hodaviah.4, and automatically changing either record would silently choose a debated textual/genealogical reconstruction. Keep both source-based candidates as explicitly unresolved in v0.1; do not introduce a Judah.7 link or invent a different word.

cases.reason: Nehemiah 12:8 names a Levite יְהוּדָה (Judah) in a list associated with the return under Zerubbabel; no Hebrew Hodiah is written at this location. The source links both the named Judah.7 record and Hodiah.2 (whose other source verses include Nehemiah 8:7, 9:5, 10:11). Commentators disagree whether the earlier Judah is the later Hodiah/Hodijah, a manuscript/transmission variant, or an unrelated individual/family of a different generation. Neither a silent alias merge nor deletion of the source Hodiah.2 claim is textually certain. Preserve both as distinct candidates flagged unresolved in v0.1, with no assertion that they are the same person.
